- Model tends to overestimate prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes.
- Forecast often peaks too early or too high, then underestimates the subsequent correction or continuation.
- Model shows persistent bias toward higher values in the 30-day horizon, particularly when recent history includes strong upward momentum.
- Overshoots are common after sharp price increases; model fails to account for mean reversion or volatility decay.
- Model underestimates late-period price movements, especially when true values show sustained upward trend or late-stage correction.
- Forecast exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops; often takes 2–3 days to adjust downward.
- Model overreacts to short-term volatility, leading to exaggerated peaks or troughs in forecasted 30-day series.
- When true values show strong upward momentum, model tends to underestimate the magnitude of the rise, especially in the final 10–15 days of the forecast window.
